item.title: Surfing’s elite are coming to Raglan. But I was there when a great slipped in to ride our waves
item.description: The world’s best surfers will descend on Raglan in May for the World Surf League Championship Tour. item.title: How NZ’s own laser kiwi influenced this viral anti-Ice flag in Minnesota
item.description: Over a decade on from New Zealand’s flag referendum, the influence of cult favourite laser kiwi continues to be felt around the world. Some say that if you fired a laser beam into space, it would continue to travel on and on, for ever and ever, until it hit something. But we need not look to the cosmos to find a laser beam so enduring, so powerful that it has already traversed time and space, and made history several times over. item.title: To show or no? A short history of prime ministers at Waitangi in election year
item.description: Luxon will be there tomorrow, but how often have his predecessors taken part? The political centrepiece of the annual Waitangi festivities takes place tomorrow with the pōwhiri on the upper grounds, and Christopher Luxon will be there. He’ll rock up with politicians from across the country and across parties to mark 186 years since the treaty signing and test his oratorical chops. item.description: “I’ve been driving trucks since the early 80s,” says Gee Goff. He’s up early today, before the sun even, picking up some big boxes of kale. item.title: Did Māori cede sovereignty? The historical answer is clearer than politics allows
item.description: The treaty debate has become a battlefield of ideology. The historical record tells a more disciplined – and less convenient – story. Historians like to hedge their bets. As the past is never fully recoverable, we can only make meaning from the surviving fragments.
